summary: This program shows Java's boolean type, which holds only true or false. It creates booleans directly, derives them from number comparisons, and combines them with logical operators, printing each result.

lines.text: A boolean variable has exactly two possible values, true and false, written as bare keywords with no quotation marks.

A comparison is itself an expression that produces a boolean, so the result of == can be stored in a variable rather than tested immediately. Note that == compares values while a single = assigns, which is a common slip.
The ! operator flips a boolean to its opposite and && produces true only when both sides are true, so this variable means that not everything passed but something did.
Several conditions can be chained with && to form a single yes-or-no answer; because allPassed is false here, readyToSubmit is false no matter what the other two say.
Joining a boolean to a string with + converts it automatically to the text true or false, which is how the program reports its results without any if statement.
